Need to search first.I don't have any notes on Isaiah 53 for you yet. I wasn't able to read any of the sources, so I have nothing I can back up with a page URL.

My first try fetched the pages directly: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes. The tool refused, because it only opens pages that have first come up in a search. My second try ran 17 searches, but by then I had used up all my tool calls for this turn, so none of them ran.

I could write commentary on this chapter from memory, but your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I've written nothing rather than give you notes I can't source.

**Next turn,** reply "continue" and I'll run the searches first, then read what they turn up:
- **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
  - **v. 4–5:** whether "by His stripes we are healed" includes physical healing. Sources would be Assemblies of God (ag.org) and Sam Storms against Got Questions, Grace to You (gty.org) and Desiring God.
  - **v. 5, 10:** penal substitution. Reformed and Baptist sources, plus 1517 and LCMS for the Lutheran view.
  - **v. 11:** how the Servant "justifies many."
  - **Whole chapter:** Wesley's notes for the Methodist view.
- **Other views:**
  - Bible Odyssey and NET Bible notes on whether the Servant is Israel or an individual, and on the wording of v. 8–11.
  - catholic.com, New Advent and oca.org for Catholic and Orthodox readings.
  - What these sites say about word-of-faith and healing-in-the-atonement teaching.

If you'd rather get results sooner, I can do the job in two or three smaller batches, such as verses 1–6 first and then verses 7–12.
